routines.edgeAssessment: J2000, midnight transitions, historical eras, truncation and signed output lengths cover the complete calendar string. The native test also checks the negative finite-double extreme.
routines.errorAssessment: Output capacities below two signal STRINGTOOSHORT. Positive excess capacity is bounded at the internal 180-byte date plus NUL.

routines.semantics: Parse a legacy UTC calendar, ordinal or Julian date to TDB seconds past J2000 using the loaded leap-second and conversion constants. Honor TPARCH and TSETYR; UTC2ET rejects timezone, AM/PM and alternate time systems.

Three successive UTC instants include an inserted second before 2017. Compare all observable workflow outputs to the independent implementation.
Nonintegral seconds and mixed date formats yield distinguishable ET. Compare all observable workflow outputs to the independent implementation.
Recognized UTC without required leap seconds signals a missing kernel. Require diagnostic NOLEAPSECONDS.
Observe the legacy UTC parser diagnostic for empty. Require diagnostic EMPTYSTRING.
Observe the legacy UTC parser diagnostic for label. Require diagnostic INVALIDTIMESTRING.
Observe the legacy UTC parser diagnostic for text. Require diagnostic INVALIDTIMESTRING.
Observe the legacy UTC parser diagnostic for timezone. Require diagnostic INVALIDTIMESTRING.

routines.edgeAssessment: Reference epochs, one-second leap transitions, alternate calendar spellings and fractional seconds exercise the numerical result. Bounded native tests check calendar-day, leap-table and expanded-year limits and diagnostic precedence.
routines.errorAssessment: NOLEAPSECONDS, EMPTYSTRING and INVALIDTIMESTRING remain toolkit errors. Unsafe integer narrowing or signed date/LSK arithmetic is a wrapper error.

routines.semantics: Compute apparent local solar time from the body-to-Sun LT+S state in the body-fixed frame, surface longitude and rotation sense. Return all three integer fields and the 24-hour and AM/PM strings. The Sun centric shortcut returns noon.

scenarios.observes: The Sun has noon solar time for every planetocentric longitude without any supplied kernels. Compare all observable workflow outputs to the independent implementation.
Truncate time and AM/PM independently while preserving numeric components. Compare all observable workflow outputs to the independent implementation.
Compare all five components at signed east and west longitudes, modulo a full rotation. Compare all observable workflow outputs to the independent implementation.
Sun and synthetic body have independently evolving positions at separated ET instants. Compare all observable workflow outputs to the independent implementation.
Longitude definition and the sign of the PM rate affect direction and reported solar time. Compare all observable workflow outputs to the independent implementation.
